Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 62, verse 9–10 (part 1 of 2):

The day is called al-Jumu'ah (Friday) because it is derived from al-jam' (gathering), for the people of Islam gather on it once every week in the great mosques. On it the creation of all things was completed, for it is the sixth day of the six days in which Allah created the heavens and the earth. On it Adam was created, on it he was admitted into Paradise, and on it he was expelled from it. On it the Hour will come. And there is an hour on it in which no believing servant who asks Allah for some good will coincide with it except that Allah gives it to him, as the sound ahadith establish. When He had restricted them in their dealings after the call and commanded them to gather, He permitted them, after finishing, to disperse through the land and seek Allah's bounty. Likewise, 'Urak ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, when he had prayed the Friday prayer, would leave and stand at the door of the mosque and say: "O Allah, I have answered Your call, prayed Your obligation, and dispersed as You commanded me, so provide me from Your bounty, for You are the best of providers." Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it.
It is also reported from one of the early predecessors (salaf) that he said: "Whoever buys and sells on Friday after the prayer, Allah will bless him seventy times," based on the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Then when the prayer is concluded, disperse within the land and seek of Allah's bounty﴾.
* *
And His saying: ﴿And remember Allah much, that you may be successful﴾, meaning: during your buying and selling, your taking and giving, remember Allah much, and do not let the world distract you from that which benefits you in the Abode of the Hereafter. For this reason, a hadith has come: "Whoever enters one of the markets and says: 'There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner. To Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs all praise, and He is over all things competent,' one million good deeds will be recorded for him, and one million evil deeds will be erased from him."[[Narrated from the hadith of Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him. Imam Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad (1/47), al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan, no. (8243), and Ibn Majah in al-Sunan, no. (2235). al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a gharib hadith."]]
Mujahid said: "A servant is not among those who remember Allah much until he remembers Allah standing, sitting, and lying on his side."

The Most High rebukes them for what had occurred: turning away from the khutbah (sermon) on Friday toward the trade caravan that had arrived in Madinah that day. He says: ﴿And when they see a trade or a diversion, they rush to it and leave you standing.﴾ That is, standing on the minbar (pulpit) delivering the sermon. This is how a number of the Tabi'un (the Successors) reported it, among them Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Hasan, Zayd ibn Aslam, and Qatadah.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan claimed that the trade belonged to Dihyah ibn Khalifah before he embraced Islam, and that it carried a drum (tabl), so they went off to it and left the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) standing on the minbar, except for a few of them. This report is also authentically transmitted. Imam Ahmad said:

Ibn Idris related to us, from Husayn, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Jabir who said: A caravan arrived at Madinah while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was delivering the khutbah, so the people went out and only twelve men remained, and this verse was revealed: ﴿And when they see a trade or a diversion, they rush to it.﴾

Both Bukhari and Muslim recorded it in their Sahihs, through the narration of Salim, with the same wording (al-Musnad 3/313; Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4899; Sahih Muslim no. 863).

The Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Zakariyya ibn Yahya related to us, Hushaym related to us, from Husayn, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd and Abu Sufyan, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah who said: While the Prophet (ﷺ) was delivering the khutbah on Friday, a caravan came to Madinah, and the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) hastened toward it until only twelve men remained with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, had you followed one another until none of you remained, the valley would have flowed with fire upon you." And this verse was revealed: ﴿And when they see a trade or a diversion, they rush to it and leave you standing.﴾ He also said: Among the twelve who remained firm with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) were Abu Bakr and 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both (Musnad Abi Ya'la 3/468).

In His words ﴿and leave you standing﴾ there is evidence that the imam delivers the khutbah standing on Friday. Muslim also recorded in his Sahih from Jabir ibn Samurah who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) had two khutbahs, sitting between them, reciting the Qur'an and reminding the people.

However, there is something that should be known: it has been said that this incident occurred at the time when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to place the prayer before the khutbah on Friday, as Abu Dawud related in Kitab al-Maraasil: Mahmud ibn Khalid related to us, from al-Walid, Abu Mu'adh Bukayr ibn Ma'ruf informed me that he heard Muqatil ibn Hayyan say: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to pray on Friday before the khutbah, like the two 'Eids. Then one day, while the Prophet (ﷺ) was delivering the khutbah, having already led the Friday prayer, a man entered and said: Dihyah ibn Khalifah has arrived with a trade (ﷺ)..." meaning: so they dispersed, and only a small group remained with him (al-Maraasil no. 62).

* *

As for His words ﴿Say: What is with Allah is better than diversion and than trade, and Allah is the best of providers﴾: that is, what Allah has of reward in the Hereafter is better, and Allah is the best of providers for those who put their trust in Him and seek provision at its proper time.
